svg.aria-label: How a less-than character breaks out and turns data into a running script in the Week 5 hello page, and how output encoding stops it. Row one, normal input name equals you: the page is h1 Hello, you exclamation close-h1; the word you sits between the tags as text, so the browser renders Hello, you. Row two, injected input name equals script alert 1 close-script: the page becomes h1 Hello, then a real script tag containing alert 1, then close-h1; the user's less-than opens a genuine tag, so the browser parses it as a script element and executes alert 1 in the site's own origin — this is where data became code, the same break-out as a quote in SQL injection. Row three, the fix, escape on output: the value is encoded so less-than becomes ampersand l t semicolon and greater-than becomes ampersand g t semicolon; the browser reads those as HTML entities, which are text and not a tag start, so it displays the literal characters script alert 1 close-script on the page and runs nothing. Bottom line: XSS is a bug on output, not input; encode the data for the context it lands in — HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, or URL each need different encoding — so that a less-than can never start a tag. The script is shown, not run.
svg.title: The < breaks out — how one character turns data into a running script, and how output encoding stops it (Week 5, CWE-79)
svg.text: The < breaks out — one character turns data into a running script
Week 5 · Cross-Site Scripting · CWE-79 · the /hello page in vulnerable_app.py
The value sits between the tags as text — the browser just displays it.
Your < opens a real tag — the browser parses <script> and runs it, in the site's origin.
→ executes alert(1) · can read document.cookie, rewrite the page, act as the victim
③ The fix — escape() on output
< is an HTML entity — the parser reads it as text, not a tag-start.
→ the browser shows the characters; nothing runs · data stays data
XSS is a bug on output, not input — storing <script> is fine; rendering it unescaped is the bug.
Encode the value for the context it lands in — HTML body, attribute, JavaScript, or URL each need
different encoding — so a < can never start a tag. Cookie flags & CSP are extra layers, not the fix.
fix: fixed_app.py L21 (escape reflected) · L29-33 (Jinja autoescape, stored) · L12 (CSP, defense-in-depth)
